Unit 1 of 10: The Portrait of a Lady

Key ideas

  • Author: Khushwant Singh. A memoir of his grandmother.
  • Village phase: she woke him, got him ready for school, went with him to the school attached to the temple, read scriptures while he studied, and fed the village dogs with stale chapatis on the way home. Their friendship was close.
  • City phase: they moved to the city; he went to an English school by bus. She could not help with lessons and disliked that there was no teaching about God and scriptures. She was upset to hear music was taught — to her it was for beggars and prostitutes. They drifted apart; she fed sparrows in the courtyard.
  • University and abroad: he got a room of his own; she accepted her seclusion. When he went abroad for five years, she saw him off at the station silently, praying.
  • Return and death: on his return she celebrated by singing with the neighbourhood women, beating a drum — for once she skipped her prayers. Next day she fell ill, refused to stop praying, and died peacefully. Thousands of sparrows sat silently around her body and ignored the crumbs; they flew away after she was carried off.
  • Themes: generation gap; changing relationships; faith and serenity; love beyond words.

Worked examples

Example 1: Why did the grandmother stop going to school with the author in the city? Answer: he went to an English school by motor bus, so she couldn't accompany him; she also couldn't help with English, science or music lessons.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) In the village, the grandmother fed: (a) sparrows (b) street dogs (c) cows (d) pigeons. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) What did the grandmother do on the evening the author returned from abroad? Answer: she sang with the women of the neighbourhood, beating an old drum.
  3. (2 marks) Why did the grandmother disapprove of music lessons? Answer: she linked music with beggars and prostitutes, not gentlefolk (1); she felt school should teach about God and scriptures (1).
  4. (3 marks) Describe the sparrows' behaviour after the grandmother's death. Answer: thousands sat silently around her body (1); they didn't touch the bread crumbs thrown to them (1); they flew away quietly after the body was carried off — a sign of mourning (1).
  5. (3 marks) Trace three stages of the author's relationship with his grandmother. Answer: village — close friends (1); city — growing distance (1); university — accepted seclusion, yet deep love shown at the end (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Sparrows in the village (they're in the city). 2. Dogs in the city. 3. Missing the skipped prayers. 4. Calling her bitter — she was serene. 5. Quoting lines instead of explaining.

Quick recall

  1. Author? 2. Village school attached to? 3. City-phase pets? 4. Years abroad? 5. Sign of her death's significance?

Answers: 1) Khushwant Singh. 2) Temple. 3) Sparrows. 4) Five. 5) Silent sparrows.
